title: Donut Trellis — Subset Mode (Binary Decomposition by Category)

complexity.rationale: Scope narrowed to the per-panel binary-decomposition data derivation (panel grid layout is now donut-trellis-grid-layout's shared concern, consumed here rather than built here). Confirmed with the user this is part of the same `trellis` feature family as donut-trellis (category mode), not an unrelated feature - but the per-panel data derivation is genuinely different and still real new logic: deriving N independent 2-row 'this category vs. everything else' datasets from one categorical field, akin to running the existing isBoolean pie-transform once per unique category value. The exact mechanism for selecting subset mode (vs. category mode) within the shared `trellis` prop family is still an open question, but it's a design decision to confirm, not a deep unknown.

summary: Donut Trellis Subset Mode is one of two modes of the same not-yet-built `trellis` feature (the other, category mode, is donut-trellis) - confirmed by the user that both are 'trellis,' just with different data derivation. Subset mode decomposes ONE existing categorical field into N separate binary (highlighted-vs-rest) donuts, one per unique category value - each panel highlights that single category's own color against the rest of the data grouped into a shared gray 'other' segment. Confirmed via a live Figma reference (a 'Big one'/'Trellis' toggle demonstrating this as an alternate presentation of the same single-donut data: Phone/Tablet/Desktop/Watch, one binary donut per device category, each showing that category's value/percent inside and its name as a title below). Matches donut-chart-tokens' documented 'Small multiple binary donut (S/M/L)' component set. Unlike category mode - which facets by an independent field and repeats the full multi-segment donut per value - subset mode has no separate trellis field; each panel is a generated 2-row subset of the same field already driving the donut's segmentation. Panel grid positioning is shared infrastructure tracked in donut-trellis-grid-layout.
requirements: Given the same categorical field a normal Donut already uses for `color`, auto-generate N small binary donuts, one per unique value in that field - each panel highlights that ONE category's own categorical color against the rest of the data grouped into a shared gray 'other' segment (chart.donut.color.secondary-gray, #C6C6C6/gray-400).

Each panel's center shows the value/percent of only that category (e.g. '65.2%' for Phone) - confirmed as a single line (value only, no separate metric-label line) in this reference, simpler than the standard DonutSummary.
Each panel's title (below it, using donut-trellis-grid-layout's shared mechanism) shows the category name (e.g. 'Phone', 'Tablet').

This mode and category mode (donut-trellis) are both part of the same `trellis` prop family, per the user - not two unrelated features. They need genuinely different per-panel data-derivation logic (category mode facets an independent field and keeps each facet's own rows; subset mode derives a 2-row this-vs-rest dataset per value of the donut's own color field), but share the same grid-layout mechanism (donut-trellis-grid-layout) and ideally the same prop namespace (see openQuestions in both specs).

The 'Big one' vs. 'Trellis' segmented control shown in the reference is a UI affordance in the Figma mockup demonstrating two presentations of the same data - unclear whether RSC needs to expose a built-in toggle, or whether choosing between a normal `<Donut>` and this subset mode is purely up to the consuming application (see openQuestions).
